response.rationale: “Lajang” is the ordinary Indonesian term for unmarried, while Malaysian Malay commonly uses “bujang” for the same relationship status. The forms provide a useful everyday variety contrast, though “bujang” can sometimes suggest a bachelor.
response.risk_rationale: “Bujang” may carry a male/bachelor nuance in some contexts, whereas “lajang” is more gender-neutral.
response.shared_synonym_rationale: “Single” is understood and used colloquially in both varieties, but “lajang” and “bujang” remain credible ordinary preferences in Indonesian and Malaysian Malay respectively.
